dross-task-writer agent definition (edit task files, scoped tests, bounded dross-writer-report) and its one-line spawn prompt

dross task dispatch sums task.files bytes at HEAD and routes solo tasks at or above writerSurfaceBytes to dross-task-writer unless the writerEnabled kill switch is off; compareKillSwitch judges the trial on above-gate medians
fences the writer to its task files and read-only commands, refuses zombie writers, and keeps the main loop off a writer-owned task

findings.text: writer_resume_post.json holds a SubagentStop, not a PostToolUse; the name comes from the task record, but it may mislead later readers

In the capture (headless, permission_mode acceptEdits) the writer's Bash was denied, so both writer reports say 'test: not run'. PreToolUse still fired, so the go/no-go holds. A real solo writer needs Bash to run tests, or every writer report comes back not-green; worth checking before t-8/t-9 rely on it

No canary or isolation test covers the writer fixtures the way TestCapturedStopIsolation covers the reviewer stop. The description's grep for CLAUDE.md lines is a manual step that this diff cannot show was done

TestKillSwitchCopiesNoContent accepts the allowed key names (method, filter, status, phase, task) at any depth, so transcript text stored under one of those names inside a [[before.task]] row or any other table would still pass. Tying each allowed key to the table it belongs in would close that gap.

kill-switch.toml is excluded from the review diff as .dross/ bookkeeping, so its rows, jq filter and calibration values (provisional 50,000 bytes) could not be checked here. The five tests are the only guard on its content.
v17SoloPhases hardcodes five phases as the solo-task-review to review-comment-ingest range. If a v1.7 solo phase is missing from the list, the baseline check will not catch it.
TestWriterDefinitionShape's banned-tool loop can never fire independently: the exact slices.Equal against the six-tool list already rejects any addition
the frontmatter parser in writerDef skips indented lines, so a YAML block-list tools: value parses as empty; the test still fails in that case (Fatal on empty tools), so coverage holds
the body's 'If the suite is red' means the scoped `dross test --files` run, not the full suite, which the same section forbids; the wording could be tightened to 'scoped tests'

TestAgentGatePairSentenceStable matches the pair text followed by a space, so it depends on the exception sentence (or something) following the pair text. If the amendment were removed, the pair-stability test would also fail, even though the pair text itself would be unchanged.

The existing line in the audit doc's execute section, 'implementation, edits and commits stay in the main loop', is now qualified only by the next paragraph ('Under --solo ... goes further'). It reads correctly, but a reader skimming only that sentence could miss the solo exception.

releaseTaskWriter clears writer.json before plan.Save; if the plan save then fails, the record is gone while the task is not pending, so the zombie-writer fence is lost for a task that was never actually reset. Clearing after a successful Save would close this.

A corrupt or tracked writer.json makes every `task status ... pending` fail, even for tasks the record does not name, because LoadWriter's error is returned before the phase/task comparison. This fails closed, which fits the guard's intent, but it blocks unrelated resets until the file is repaired.
The tamper-guard doc comment in internal/gate/override.go now has one line well past the surrounding wrap width.

judgeWriterSpawn and the launch recorder compare strings.TrimSpace(prompt) to WriterPromptLine, so leading or trailing whitespace is admitted despite the 'exactly' wording; this is harmless, and appended text is still refused as the contract requires

the recorder also re-arms the record to launched on a SendMessage to the bound agent, which the task description does not mention; TestWriterStopClearsGreen and TestWriterStopIgnoresUnbound cover it, so it is tested, not dead

writerTask's last reason, 'HEAD is not on phase/<id>', is reached by ruling out the other causes rather than by checking the branch itself; it is correct for every path ArmedScope currently has, but a new nil-return cause added to ArmedScope later would be misreported as off-branch

writerCommandRefusal admits `dross task …`/`dross rule …` whenever any arg equals "show" (slices.Contains(args, "show")), so `dross task status p t-1 failed --reason show` passes the writer fence and sets task status; check the verb right after task/rule instead

solo-writer is Workflow-scoped and the root comes from the file's directory, so a writer Edit/Write to a path outside any dross repo (e.g. under ~/.claude) gets root "" and is let through before judgeWriterEdit runs; the intended 'not one of the task's files' refusal never fires and no test covers it

judgeMainLoop does not refuse a partially-read script while the writer is launched, so a main-loop `sh -c 'git commit -m x'` or `eval "dross test"` gets past the wait-for-completion fence; the writer side fails closed on the same input

the gate now claims every main-loop Bash/Edit call; any load error (damaged writer.json/execute.json, or ArmedScope's ambiguous multiple-in-progress error while a writer record exists) refuses all of them, including the commands that would repair state, until a human lifts the gate
tests use the captured writer/main-loop fixtures and run only the solo-writer gate, so admits/refusals are attributable to this fence; TestNoInlineTakeover covers both launched and stopped states

The writer's Bash fence blocks a list of known commands and lets everything else through. Wrapper commands get past it. shellscan only unwraps env/command/sudo/nohup/time, and it deliberately leaves `env -S` as written, so `env -S 'git commit -m x'`, `timeout 5 git commit -m x`, `nice git commit -m x` and `stdbuf -o0 git commit` all reach a program name the fence doesn't list and are admitted. So are interpreters and build tools that can run anything (`python3 -c`, `perl -e` without -i, `awk 'BEGIN{system(...)}'`, `make`). Adding env/timeout/nice/stdbuf to writerOpaque would close the cheapest of these.

claimsSoloWriter claims every Bash, Edit and Write the main loop makes. When a solo writer record exists, any load error is returned to the engine: a damaged writer.json, an undecodable plan.toml, or ArmedScope's ambiguous-tasks error. If the engine refuses on judge errors (fail closed), that also blocks the escape route this task promises always passes: the stash and `dross task status … failed`. The gate can be lifted, so a human can recover.

The inline-takeover fence covers only the Edit and Write family of tools. The main loop can still change a writer-owned task's code through Bash, for example `sed -i … a.go`, `cp`, `echo > a.go` or `git checkout -- a.go`. That is within what the description claims, but it leaves an easy way round c-5.

Two checks find the dross verb differently. The main-loop wait check reads args[0] (`args[0] == "test"`, `args[1] == "context"`). The writer check takes the first word that isn't a flag. If dross ever accepts a global flag before the verb, `dross --flag test` would get past the main-loop wait.
`git -c alias.x='!…' <read-sub>` and `git -c core.pager=…` with an allowed read subcommand can run arbitrary commands. Low risk, but the fence doesn't account for them.
